criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked all numbered YED-149 decisions against the implementation. The retry/NotSent behavior and read-cache scoping are mostly aligned, but decision 1 is contradicted: a missing page id does not hard-fail the batch immediately; the code keeps processing and only returns 3 after the loop. That is a real spec-drift correctness issue.

The patch includes the relevant production changes plus selftests for the new retry and refusal behaviors, and the supplied reference checks report no missing load-bearing files. The only nit is that the refusal test is single-row and does not exercise the more dangerous multi-row batch case, but the required pieces are present.

I checked placement, naming, and the house conventions called out in the prompt. The changes stay in `.claude/scripts/`, do not violate the alex-prefix skill rule, and do not show an MCP/fan-out or parent-thread write-path break. No major convention violation stood out; this is basically clean with a small review nit around the extra presentation state.

The connection reuse and table-scoped invalidation are lean and purposeful, but the new `_made_names` side list does duplicate state for reporting. That is a small anti-pattern smell rather than a platform-building or tombstone-resurrection problem, so this lands in the good-but-not-perfect band.

The failure messages and selftest additions are fairly legible, but the narrative section asserts measured timings and stall rates as settled facts without provenance in the artifact. That hurts honesty/confidence even though the operational errors are otherwise specific.

defects.quote: print(f"ensure-roles: {refused} row(s) REFUSED for a missing/invalid page id — every other row was processed; exit 3")
defects.description: Decision 1 says "A `role_posted` manifest with no page id is a hard failure." This implementation keeps processing later rows and only exits 3 at the end, so invalid input can still produce partial writes before the run fails.

defects.quote: self._made_names = getattr(self, "_made_names", []) + [(table, name)]   # display casing, for review output
defects.description: This introduces a second mutable list tracking the same creation events as `_made`, solely for display casing. That duplicates state and creates a drift risk between the canonical record and the review-only shadow copy.

defects.quote: Measured (Fable diagnosis): ~10% of FRESH TCP connects from this network stall on SYN (all hosts).
defects.description: The artifact presents performance measurements and run results as established fact without any source or citation in the artifact itself. Under the rubric, that is overclaiming certainty / honesty, even if the code changes may still be sound.
